title: The Almanack of Naval Ravikant
author: Eric Jorgenson
blurb: Eric Jorgenson gathered years of Naval Ravikant's tweets, podcast conversations and essays and organized them into one short guide. Naval is an entrepreneur and investor best known for cofounding AngelList. The book has two halves. The first is about wealth. Naval argues that getting rich is a learnable skill, not luck. It comes from owning assets, building specific knowledge that others can't easily copy, using leverage like code and media, and taking accountability for your work. The second half is about happiness. Naval treats happiness as a skill too, built through habits like meditation, reading, exercise and letting go of endless desire. The thread connecting both halves is freedom. Wealth buys freedom from having to work. Inner peace frees you from your own restless mind.

lessons.t: Getting rich is a skill, not luck
lessons.b: Seek wealth, meaning assets that earn while you sleep, rather than chasing a salary or status, because wealth creation is a positive-sum game anyone can learn.
Your edge is knowledge that can't be taught in a classroom, found by following your genuine curiosity toward work that feels like play to you but looks like work to others.

lessons.t: Use leverage that needs no permission
lessons.b: Code and media multiply your effort without anyone's permission, letting one person's work reach millions while they sleep.
issues: scene 2: The dashed 'messy' curve sweeps down to the caption's baseline. Its lower loop runs right up against the end of 'Messy: the worst form of leverage.', so the line nearly collides with the caption text. (fix: Keep the dashed path inside the people grid (bottom no lower than about y=780 at 1600x900), or move the caption down/left so there is at least 30px clearance from the curve.)

lessons.b: Putting your name on your work and owning the results earns trust and rewards, and with leverage, good judgment becomes the most valuable skill you can have.
issues: scene 3: The rising bar chart in the bottom right runs down almost to the 'visualgrowth.app' footer, so the tallest bars nearly touch the footer text. The dark rounded bar sticking out left of the podium also reads as a stray, unexplained shape. (fix: Shrink the bar chart and raise its baseline (to about y≤800 at 1600x900) so it clears the footer by at least 40px. Remove the dark bar beside the podium, or replace it with a clearly recognisable element.)

scene 7: The 'NO SHORTCUT' drawing (a table with a lever-like bar and an amber block under a crossed-out arc) is hard to read and does not clearly show skipping effort. (fix: Redraw it as a clear metaphor, for example a path with a dashed jump arc marked with an X over a staircase of steps, so 'no shortcut around effort' is obvious.)

lessons.t: Play long-term games with long-term people
lessons.b: The biggest returns in money, relationships and reputation come from compounding over years with people you trust.

lessons.t: Happiness is a skill you can train
lessons.b: Happiness is mostly a state of peace you can cultivate, and every desire is a contract you make with yourself to be unhappy until you get it.
issues: scene 4: The 'SOMETHING MISSING' cloud and its label are faded almost to invisibility. They sit cramped just under the subtitle, far from the person they belong to. The narration's key beat, the cloud that follows you, is effectively unreadable. (fix: Place the cloud directly above the person's head, below the subtitle with at least 40px clearance. Keep the label at full muted grey-blue contrast. If the cloud should show as lifted, fade only the cloud shape, or move it upward and away, but keep the label legible.)

scene 6: The 'WANT' text inside the small craving envelopes overlaps the envelope flap lines and is illegible. It is also far below 18px. The 'SMALL CRAVINGS' and 'LET GO' labels are faded too low to read. (fix: Remove the text from the envelopes, or enlarge the envelopes so 'WANT' sits clear of the flap lines at 18px or more. Raise the 'SMALL CRAVINGS' and 'LET GO' labels to readable muted grey-blue opacity.)

scene 2: The 'WHAT WE PICTURE' and 'EXCITEMENT · BIG WINS' labels in the left panel are dimmed to very low contrast and barely readable. (fix: Keep the left panel's drawing dimmed but render its labels in the standard muted grey-blue at full opacity, so the comparison stays readable.)

lessons.t: Wealth and peace both buy freedom
lessons.b: Productize yourself to earn freedom from forced work, and build habits like meditation, reading and exercise to earn freedom from your own restless mind.
